segments.text: This is PACT. It's a drone delivery fleet that keeps working, even when the central brain goes dark.

Right now, most delivery fleets lean on one central controller and a solid radio link. If you lose that hub, every drone stops. And if the radio splits, two groups of drones can end up claiming the same parcel.

PACT gets rid of the central controller. Every drone runs the same logic, and it only talks to the drones it can actually reach by radio. They bid for jobs based on priority, distance, deadline and battery. Each drone keeps its own copy of the order board, and those copies sync up by gossip.

So here's the same city, the same seed and the same orders, run twice. On the left, a central hub hands out every job. Three minutes in, we kill the hub. The central fleet stops picking up new work. PACT doesn't have anything central to lose, so it just keeps going: eighty-six percent on time, the same as with no fault at all.

Now let's split the fleet in two over the radio, for five minutes. Both halves keep working, and every claim carries an epoch and a lease, so a depot only hands a parcel to its newest owner. Across two hundred and forty runs with radio splits, PACT made zero double deliveries. A plain auction made nearly eighteen per run.
And when the radio splits the fleet, across two hundred and forty runs, PACT made zero double deliveries.

If a drone fails mid-delivery, it just goes quiet. The drones that were expecting to hear from it report the silence, its depot marks it as failed, and exactly one replacement job goes out to auction.

And it's not just a browser demo. The same protocol runs as real robotics software: ROS 2 lifecycle components, one container per drone, quadrotor physics in Gazebo, and PX4 autopilots in the loop, all over an authenticated mesh radio.

Every run is deterministic. The same seed gives you the same event log, and the replay viewer checks it event by event. Nearly a thousand automated tests pass across both simulators, and there's a public benchmark against three baselines.
Today, PACT is a simulation prototype, and real hardware is the next step. No hub, no double deliveries, no stalls.
